rows: Mean CFO / net profit 112% over 5 years
5 FLAG / 3 WATCH across 16 accounting tests; LojikX™ Consistency Score 30/100

sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Inventory vs. Sales / COGS Trend: Inventory intensity changed +5.7 percentage points of total assets and inventory days moved -2 days. Stock is building faster than sales, a classic early warning of demand weakness or channel stuffing.
FCF Generation Consistency: Free cash flow was positive in 1 of the last 5 reported years. Repeated FCF deficits mean growth is being funded by the balance sheet rather than by the business.
Gross Margin Stability: Gross margin varied with a standard deviation of 10.7 percentage points. Margin volatility suggests commodity exposure or weak pricing power.
Operating Margin Stability: Operating margin standard deviation of 20.2 pp indicates cost swings that make forecasting unreliable.
Share Dilution Check: The share count changed +4.8% a year. Dilution transfers value from existing holders to new issuance.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of 2.0% with ROE of 1.2% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
CapEx Intensity Check: Capital expenditure averaged 12.7% of revenue. Capex intensity is unusual for the business model and needs a return check.
Interest Coverage Safety: Operating profit covers interest 3.1 times. Coverage is thin enough that a profit dip would pressure debt service.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 5 hard red flags and 3 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 30/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
